subject: general
question: Which of the following national sports events is NOT associated with cricket?
solution:
The correct answer is **"Durand Cup".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Durand Cup:**

 
 
• The 131st edition of the Durand Cup, **the oldest football competition in Asia**, and the first one since it was recognised by the Asian Football Confederation were the 2022 Durand Cup, also known as the Indian Oil Durand Cup because of sponsorship connections with Indian Oil Corporation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Deodhar Trophy:

 
 
• The Deodhar Trophy, sometimes spelled Devdhar Trophy, is an Indian domestic cricket List A championship competition. It is a 50-over knockout competition that is played annually between India A, India B, and India C and is named for D B Deodhar, also referred to as the Grand Old Man of Indian Cricket. India B currently holds the title after defeating India C by 51 runs in the 2019–20 final. In 2022 it was held from 8 September.
 
 
 
• Vijay Hazare trophy:
 
 
• ​The Board of Control for Cricket in India hosts the annual domestic limited-overs cricket competition known as the Vijay Hazare Trophy, commonly known as the Ranji One-Day Trophy. It is officially known as the Mastercard Vijay Hazare Trophy due to sponsorship considerations (BCCI). In 2022, it was played from November 12 to December 2 with 38 teams.
 
 
 
• Ranji trophy:
 
 
• The Ranji Trophy is a domestic first-class cricket championship played in India involving numerous teams representing regional and state cricket bodies. It is sometimes known as the Mastercard Ranji Trophy due to sponsorship reasons. Ranji Trophy was established in 1935 by the Board of Control for Cricket in India, and since then it has been held yearly on different Indian grounds and stadiums. In 2022, it was played from December 13 to February 19.
